{{about|the finite case}} == Theorem == <onlyinclude> Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] and let $H$ be a [[Definition:Subgroup|subgroup]] of $G$.
Then the '''order''' of $H$ is a [[Definition:Divisor of Integer|divisor]] of the order of $G$.<ref>A note.</ref> </onlyinclude>
== [[Order of Subgroup Divides Order of Group/Proof 1|Proof 1]] == {{:Order of Subgroup Divides Order of Group/Proof 1}}
== Sources == * {{BookReference|A Book|1965|An Author}}: Theorem 25.6

== Definition == The '''centre''' of a [[Definition:Group|group]] $G$ is the set of the elements of $G$ that commute with all the elements of $G$: $\set {x \in G: \forall g \in G: x g = g x}$ <!-- a comment that is not text --> == Sources == * A book that has the definition, in its third chapter, on its first page.
[[Category:Definitions/Group Theory]]
== Axiom == <onlyinclude>The product of two elements of the structure is again an element of the structure.</onlyinclude> [[Category:Axioms/Group Theory]]
== Puzzle == Find all the groups of order four up to isomorphism, and show that there are two of them.
